prompt.brief: Design an NLP platform that processes unstructured text through normalization, language detection, entity and relation extraction, sentiment, topic modeling, and classification with versioned outputs.
successSignals: Keep source text immutable and version processors, model artifacts, tokenization, annotations, confidence, and schema mappings.
Support streaming and batch modes with bounded document work, tenant quotas, language-aware models, and deterministic retries.
Return spans and relations with offsets and confidence so downstream users can inspect evidence rather than trust a label blindly.
Explain PII redaction, model drift, long documents, malformed encodings, human correction, evaluation, and replay.

functional: Submit text or documents, normalize and detect language, extract entities and relations, classify content, and store versioned annotations.
Provide batch and synchronous APIs with per-document status, confidence, model version, offsets, and processing errors.
Support redaction, correction, reprocessing, dataset export, tenant access, retention, and evaluation feedback.
nonFunctional: Target entity F1 above 90% on declared evaluation sets and keep small synchronous documents below 500 ms p95.
Process 100 million documents per day using document and tenant partitions without one long document starving the queue.
Make document submission, model inference, annotation publication, and correction events idempotent.
Fall back to a lightweight ruleset or return a partial result with confidence warnings when a model is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Process 100 million documents per day across dozens of languages and multiple domain-specific model versions.
Partition by tenant, language, document, and model; isolate long documents and high-volume producers.
Retain encrypted source text, token offsets, annotations, models, evaluation sets, and redaction audit records.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the NLP platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional NLP platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return NLP platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition NLP platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound NLP platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for NLP platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable NLP platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable NLP platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure NLP platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
